subject: mathematics
question_text: If 3A ≠ (2n + 1)π/2, prove that tan A tan(60° + A) tan(60° − A) = tan 3A, and find the value of tan 6° tan 42° tan 66° tan 78°.

mark_split.label: Use the identity twice for the value

verification.note: Source: Sri Chaitanya, FAST TRACK IPE for Jr. Students — Mathematics-IA (2026-27 edition), chapter 8 TRIGONOMETRIC RATIOS, Very Short Answer question 48, book p.96. Only the question was taken. The solution, the step order and the mark split are this answer book's own work — see docs/ORIGINALITY_MATHS.md. THE MARK SPLIT IS OURS, NOT THE BOOK'S: the Mathematics-IA volume prints no per-step mark allocation on any answer. The question asks for two things — a proof and a number — so the 1 + 1 gives one mark to each. The stem's condition was checked and is sufficient: 1 − 3tan²A = 0 forces 3A to be an odd multiple of π/2, and so does tan A or tan(60° ± A) being undefined, so the single printed inequality covers every case. Paper position: Maths-1A Section A prints ten very short answers of 2 marks each and the student writes all ten, under the 2026-27 pattern; Trigonometric Ratios and Transformations supplies two of those ten slots. This is a coaching publication, not a TSBIE document, so the split stays unverified until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it.

recall_prompt: Say how you would do this — name how you prove the identity, and which two values of A you use for the number.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Prove the product equals tan 3A
steps.margin_note: First mark. Multiply the two brackets before anything else. The numerators give 3 − tan²A and the denominators give 1 − 3tan²A, which is the tan 3A formula short of one tan A.
steps.memory_tip: tan 60° = √3. Multiply the two brackets first — what comes out is the tan 3A formula apart from one factor of tan A.
lines: 3A is not an odd multiple of π/2, so tan 3A

recall.must_convey: That the two brackets are multiplied first, giving (3 − tan²A)/(1 − 3tan²A), and that one more factor of tan A makes it the tan 3A formula.
accept: expand both brackets with tan sixty equal to root three
multiply them and you get three minus tan squared over one minus three tan squared
one more tan A gives the tan three A formula
tan sixty ante root three, rendu brackets multiply cheyyali
so the product is tan three A
reject: take A equal to six degrees

steps.why: Multiplying the two brackets first is what makes this short: the numerators give 3 − tan²A and the denominators give 1 − 3tan²A, and that pair is exactly the tan 3A formula with one factor of tan A still missing.
common_mistakes: Multiplying the numerator of one bracket by the denominator of the other.

steps.label: Use the identity twice for the value
steps.margin_note: Second mark. A = 6° gives the triple 6°, 66°, 54°; A = 18° gives 18°, 78°, 42°. The extra factors tan 54° and tan 18° are reciprocals of each other, so they cancel.
steps.memory_tip: Each printed pair sits inside one triple: 6° with 66°, and 42° with 78°. The missing members are tan 54° and tan 18°, and they cancel.
lines: Put A = 6°: tan6° tan66° tan54° = tan18°
Put A = 18°: tan18° tan78° tan42° = tan54°

recall.must_convey: That A = 6° and A = 18° are substituted into the identity and the two results multiplied, so tan 54° and tan 18° cancel and the value is 1.
accept: put A equal to six degrees and then A equal to eighteen degrees
six with sixty six gives tan eighteen over tan fifty four
forty two with seventy eight gives tan fifty four over tan eighteen
rendu results multiply cheste tan fifty four tan eighteen cancel

steps.why: The four printed angles are two of the identity's triples with one member missing from each. A = 6° leaves the extra factor tan18°/tan54° and A = 18° leaves tan54°/tan18°. Those two are reciprocals, so their product is 1.
common_mistakes: Using A = 6° only, which never produces 42° and 78°.
Leaving the answer as a ratio of tangents instead of the number 1.
